subject: Operating System
chapters: Chapter 6: File System Implementation and Storage
Chapter 7: Secondary Storage Structure and I/O Systems

questions.text: What is an Operating System? Explain OS goals, core functions as a resource manager and extended virtual machine. Compare Mainframe, Desktop, Multiprocessor, Distributed, Clustered, Real-Time, and Handheld systems.
Differentiate between Batch Systems, Multiprogrammed Systems, and Time-Sharing (Multitasking) Systems with CPU utilization and response time diagrams.
Explain Dual-Mode Operation in OS (User Mode vs Kernel Mode). Explain Mode Bit, Hardware Protection (Timer, Base & Limit Registers), and Privileged Instructions.

What are System Calls? Explain the mechanism of passing parameters to system calls (Registers, Memory Block/Table, Stack). Describe system call types (Process Control, File Management, Device Management, Information Maintenance, Communications).
Explain Operating System Architectures: Monolithic Systems, Layered Approach, Microkernels (Client-Server model, e.g. Mach), and Hybrid Kernels with architectural block diagrams.
Explain Virtual Machines and System Booting (Bootstrap loader, BIOS/UEFI, POST, MBR, GRUB kernel initialization). Compare Hypervisor Type 1 (Bare-metal) vs Type 2 (Hosted).
Define Process in OS. Explain Process State Transition Diagram (New, Ready, Running, Waiting, Terminated) and Process Control Block (PCB) attributes.

Explain Process Scheduling Queues (Job Queue, Ready Queue, Device/Waiting Queue) and Schedulers: Long-Term (Admission), Short-Term (CPU), and Medium-Term (Swapper) schedulers. Explain Context Switching overhead.
Explain Process Creation and Termination in UNIX/Linux using `fork()`, `exec()`, `wait()`, and `exit()` system calls. Differentiate between Zombie Process and Orphan Process.

Explain Threads: Single-Threaded vs Multi-Threaded processes. Compare User-Level Threads (ULT) vs Kernel-Level Threads (KLT). Describe Multithreading Models: Many-to-One, One-to-One, and Many-to-Many.
Explain CPU Scheduling Criteria (CPU Utilization, Throughput, Turnaround Time, Waiting Time, Response Time). Compare Preemptive vs Non-Preemptive scheduling.

CPU Scheduling Problem: Given 5 processes $P_1(0, 10), P_2(1, 4), P_3(2, 5), P_4(3, 2), P_5(4, 1)$ (Format: $P_i(\text{Arrival}, \text{Burst})$), draw Gantt charts and compute average waiting time and turnaround time for:
(a) FCFS,
(b) SJF (Non-preemptive),
(c) SRTF (Preemptive SJF),
(d) Round Robin ($Q = 2\text{ ms}$).
Explain Multilevel Queue Scheduling and Multilevel Feedback Queue (MLFQ) Scheduling with aging mechanisms.

What is the Critical Section Problem? State the 3 requirements for a valid solution: (1) Mutual Exclusion, (2) Progress, (3) Bounded Waiting. Explain Peterson's Algorithm for two processes and prove it satisfies all three requirements.
Explain Hardware Synchronization solutions: Test-and-Set and Swap/Compare-and-Swap atomic instructions. What is a Spinlock / Busy Waiting?

Explain Semaphores (Counting Semaphore vs Binary Semaphore) with `wait()` and `signal()` operations. Write Semaphore solutions for:
(a) Producer-Consumer (Bounded Buffer) problem,
(b) Readers-Writers problem (Reader's preference),
(c) Dining Philosophers problem.
What is a Deadlock? State and explain the 4 Coffman conditions necessary for deadlock: (1) Mutual Exclusion, (2) Hold and Wait, (3) No Preemption, (4) Circular Wait.
Explain Resource Allocation Graphs (RAG). How is deadlock detected in single-unit resource systems using cycle detection? Explain claim edges and request edges.
Explain Deadlock Prevention strategies by eliminating each of the four Coffman conditions.

Explain Banker's Algorithm for Deadlock Avoidance. Given 5 processes $P_0..P_4$ and 3 resources $A(10), B(5), C(7)$ with Allocation and Max matrices:
(a) Compute Need matrix,
(b) Determine if the system is in a safe state and find safe sequence,
(c) If $P_1$ requests $(1, 0, 2)$, can it be granted immediately?
Explain Deadlock Detection for multiple instances of resources using matrix algorithm and Deadlock Recovery methods (Process Termination vs Resource Preemption).
Explain Memory Management concepts: Logical vs Physical Address Space, Memory Management Unit (MMU), Base and Limit registers, Dynamic Loading, and Dynamic Linking.
Explain Contiguous Memory Allocation and Dynamic Partitioning. Compare Placement Strategies: First-Fit, Best-Fit, and Worst-Fit. Explain Internal vs External Fragmentation and 50% Rule.
Explain Paging memory management scheme. Explain Page Table structure, Page Size, Frame Size, and Hardware translation of Logical Address $(p, d)$ into Physical Address $(f, d)$.

Explain Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB). Calculate Effective Memory Access Time (EMAT): Given TLB hit ratio $\alpha = 80\%$, TLB access time $= 20\text{ ns}$, and main memory access time $= 100\text{ ns}$.
Explain Page Table Hierarchies: Hierarchical (Multi-level) Paging, Hashed Page Tables, and Inverted Page Tables.
Explain Segmentation memory management scheme. Describe Segment Table (Base and Limit), Segment-to-Physical Address translation, and compare Paging vs Segmentation.
Explain Virtual Memory and Demand Paging. Explain Page Fault handling sequence step-by-step with diagram. Explain Effective Access Time in Demand Paging.

Page Replacement Problem: Given page reference string: $7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, 2, 3, 0, 3, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 7, 0, 1$ with 3 and 4 memory frames. Compute total page faults using:
(a) FIFO,
(b) Optimal (OPT),
(c) Least Recently Used (LRU).
Explain Belady's Anomaly.
What is Thrashing? Explain causes of thrashing, Working-Set Model, Page Fault Frequency (PFF) control, and Locality of Reference.

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: File System Implementation and Storage
questions.text: Explain File Concept: File Attributes, File Operations, File Types, File Access Methods (Sequential vs Direct Access), and Directory Structures (Single-Level, Two-Level, Tree-Structured, Acyclic-Graph).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: File System Implementation and Storage
questions.text: Explain File Allocation Methods: Contiguous Allocation, Linked Allocation, and Indexed Allocation (UNIX inode with direct, single indirect, double indirect, triple indirect pointers).

questions.chapter: Chapter 6: File System Implementation and Storage
questions.text: Explain Free Space Management techniques: Bit Vector (Bit Map), Linked List, Grouping, and Counting.

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Secondary Storage Structure and I/O Systems
questions.text:
Disk Scheduling Problem: A hard disk has 200 cylinders (0 to 199). The queue of pending requests in FIFO order is: $98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67$. If the read/write head is currently at cylinder 53 moving towards higher numbers, calculate total head movements using:
(a) FCFS,
(b) SSTF,
(c) SCAN,
(d) C-SCAN,
(e) LOOK,
(f) C-LOOK.

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Secondary Storage Structure and I/O Systems
questions.text: Explain RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) levels: RAID 0, RAID 1, RAID 2, RAID 3, RAID 4, RAID 5 (Distributed parity), RAID 6 (Dual parity), and Nested RAID 10. Compare storage efficiency and fault tolerance.

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Secondary Storage Structure and I/O Systems
questions.text: Explain I/O Hardware: Polling (Busy waiting), Interrupts (Vectored vs Non-vectored), Direct Memory Access (DMA controller operation), and DMA transfer modes (Burst vs Cycle Stealing).

questions.chapter: Chapter 7: Secondary Storage Structure and I/O Systems
questions.text: Explain Kernel I/O Subsystem: I/O Scheduling, Buffering (Single, Double, Circular buffering), Caching, Spooling, and Device Reservation.
Explain OS Protection Mechanisms: Domain of Protection, Access Matrix, Access Control Lists (ACLs), Capability Lists, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC).
Explain Security Threats and Countermeasures: Program Threats (Trojan Horse, Trapdoor/Backdoor, Logic Bomb, Buffer Overflow) and System Threats (Worms, Viruses, DoS / DDoS attacks, Port Scanning).
